data.title: India bonds slide on RBI sales, oil-led inflation heat
data.description:
By Khushi Malhotra

Indian government bonds slumped on Tuesday, with the 10-year yield headed for its biggest one-day rise in over two months, as the central bank's planned open-market sales added to pressure from higher inflation and global rate concerns.

The benchmark 6.94% 2036 bond (IN069436G=CC) was at 7.0880% as of 11:30 a.m. IST, up 6.5 basis points from Friday's close, poised to log its biggest jump since July 8.

Bond yields move inversely to prices.

India's annual retail inflation accelerated to 4.82% in August from 4.45% in July, data on Monday showed, exceeding economists' forecast of 4.80%.

Higher inflation, driven by elevated oil prices, and rising global yields have strengthened the case for the Reserve Bank of India to start tightening policy as early as October, traders said.

Brent crude neared $110 a barrel as the Gulf war widened, while the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield breached 5%, a key threshold that risks intensifying the global debt selloff.

"The RBI's October MPC meeting is a live one, with the odds of a rate hike now much higher than earlier," analysts at Emkay Global said in a note, adding that a hike will align the central bank's liquidity and rate stance.

Traders, however, said surplus liquidity of more than 10 trillion rupees ($104.31 billion) could keep overnight rates below the RBI's policy corridor, complicating efforts to prepare markets for a near-term hike.

The RBI said on Friday it would sell 1 trillion rupees of bonds in multiple tranches over the fortnight, starting from September 17 to drain excess cash.

It has also used sell-buy swaps and variable-rate reverse repos to manage liquidity.

Focus is now on the U.S. Federal Reserve's policy decision on Wednesday.

RATES

Overnight indexed swap rates also spiked, tracking rising rate hike bets and global yields.

The one-year (INR1YMIBROIS=CC) rate was up 7 bps at 6.10%, the two-year (INR2YMIBROIS=CC) rate rose 10 bps to 6.3450%, and the liquid five-year (INR5YMIBROIS=CC) rate jumped 10 bps to 6.67%.

($1 = 95.8650 Indian rupees)

data.title: ZAWYA: Riyadh Cement seals 25-year solar power deal with Samana Energy
data.description:
By Staff Writer

Riyadh Cement Company said it had signed an agreement with Samana Energy, a leading IPP specialising in renewable energy and sustainable solutions, to purchase solar-generated electricity for a 25-year period.

Under the agreement, Riyadh Cement expects to make average annual payments of about SAR6 million ($1.6 million), excluding value-added tax, over the contract period.

The electricity would be purchased at a cost lower than its current electricity generation costs and below the cost of electricity supplied by Saudi Energy Company, said Riyadh Cement in its filing to Saudi bourse Tadawul.

Riyadh Cement would not be required to provide financing for the project and would incur no capital or operating expenditure, subject to obtaining the necessary licences and approvals from the relevant authorities, it stated.

The power generation system is expected to begin operations in Q4 2027, with cost savings expected to materialise gradually from the first year of operations, with the actual financial impact to be determined based on the energy prices applicable to the energy consumed from the project at that time, it added.

In another development, Riyadh Cement signed a partnership deal with China's Tianjin Cement Industry Design & Research Institute to implement a digital transformation project aimed at improving operational efficiency and productivity.

The 24-month contract covers the implementation of the company's "Light House Project", which will use digital technologies and Industry 4.0 applications to optimize production processes, reduce costs and improve operational performance and sustainability.

The project includes digital transformation and automation, process optimization, artificial intelligence, predictive maintenance and energy-efficiency measures, it stated.

Riyadh Cement said the project forms part of its broader operational and digital transformation strategy and is intended to strengthen its competitive position and support its long-term strategic objectives.

Also the company has inked a partnership deal with Cachapuz – Weighing & Logistics Systems for the supply, installation, and commissioning of advanced technology solutions for logistics and dispatching automation. This is aimed at further enhancing the company's dispatching operations through digital solutions and advanced safety and compliance technologies, it added.-TradeArabia News Service

data.title: LNG demand in China and India expected to recover when Mideast war ends
data.description:
Key points:
  • LNG spot price surge hits demand in India, GAIL says
  • GAIL, PetroChina traders seek alternatives to Mideast LNG
  • Chinese, Indian LNG demand to rebound once prices cool, GAIL and PetroChina expect
  • Exxon is 'extremely bullish' on long term LNG growth prospects

By Florence Tan and Emily Chow

China and India's LNG imports are likely to rebound from multi-year lows once the Middle East supply crunch ends and prices ease, industry executives expect, reversing a pick-up in coal and oil use to generate power due to the U.S.-Iran war.

The conflict has prevented Qatar and the United Arab Emirates from exporting most of their LNG via the Strait of Hormuz, where a fifth of global supplies used to pass, driving up prices and curbing demand in Asia.

Shell , the world's biggest LNG trader, estimates the world has lost about 36 million tons of LNG from the Middle East so far this year, President for Integrated Gas Cederic Cremers said.

Asia's spot prices have surged to nearly $30 per million British thermal units, from a pre-war range around $10 per MMBtu, as the region is competing with Europe for limited supplies ahead of winter.

"The prices have hit through the roof ... and that is definitely impacting the demand insofar as India is concerned because there are a lot of sectors which are price sensitive," GAIL Chairman Deepak Gupta said at the Gastech conference in Bangkok.

"There are many industries which switch over to different fuels in case gas is not viable for them," said Gupta, who heads India's top natural gas distributor by market share.

Both GAIL and PetroChina , China's top LNG importer, have deployed their trading teams to scour for alternative cargoes to replace Qatari and Emirati supplies since the war broke out.

DEMAND DESTRUCTION NOT PERMANENT

Luo Yizhou, CEO of PetroChina International (PCI), the trading arm of the state energy major, said the company was working on the Sunday of February 28 in lieu of the Lunar New Year holiday when the U.S. and Israel launched attacks on Iran.

"We had a meeting for something else, planning for this year, and then suddenly we saw the news, and then we switched the topic to how to secure supply," Luo said.

"We were probably one day ahead of the market because most of the other companies start to work on Monday."

GAIL's Gupta said India had to limit gas consumption initially but resumed supplies to almost 90% to 95% as it ramped up its trading capability to buy LNG from elsewhere.

Exxon Mobil , GAIL and PCI executives expect the Middle East conflict to have a temporary impact on demand, with consumption to rebound once prices fall and global supply recovers.

"We are hoping that all this is very short term, and in the coming days, in mid-term and long-term, things will become normal," Gupta said, adding that there may be about 150 million to 200 million tons of LNG coming online in the next four to five years which could cool prices.

"The sectors like the power sector in our country, like the various industries, they are going to go for more gas ... because it's a cleaner fuel," he said.

In China, PCI's Luo expects demand from gas-fired power plants to rebound once LNG prices return to a "normal" range of $7 to $9 per MMBtu, citing strong growth in electricity consumption even as LNG imports have fallen.

"I think it is due to the temporary suppression of the demand faced by high price," Luo said.

"I don’t think it will kill the demand in China."

Exxon expects substantial LNG demand growth in China over the long term, with extensive LNG import infrastructure built along the country's east coast, the company's vice president for global LNG marketing, Andrew Barry, told Reuters on the sidelines of the Gastech conference.

There is a lot of latent demand that is price sensitive, he said.

ExxonMobil remains confident in the diversification of its LNG portfolio, which includes assets and interests in the U.S., Mozambique, Qatar, Papua New Guinea and Australia. It continues to look at new opportunities with a focus on cost of supply.

"We still have an extremely bullish demand forecast out through to 2050," Barry said.
